key: Better than sovereignty over the earth, better than going to heaven, better than lordship over all worlds, is the reward of the first step in holiness.
s: The chapter on the world ends by setting one attainment above every kingdom and heaven; the Theravāda commentary, on verse 178, explains why: a world-ruler is still not freed from hell, but the stream-enterer has shut the doors to the states of woe.

evidence.words: Sotāpattiphalaṃ varanti yasmā ettake ṭhāne rajjaṃ kāretvāpi nirayādīhi amuttova hoti, sotāpanno pana pihitāpāyadvāro hutvā sabbadubbalopi aṭṭhame bhave na nibbattati, tasmā sotāpattiphalameva varaṃ uttamanti attho.
evidence.gloss: “The fruit of stream-entry is better”: because even one who has exercised rule over so great a domain is not freed from hell and the other lower states, whereas the stream-enterer, the doors to the states of woe shut, is not born an eighth time even if he is the weakest; therefore the fruit of stream-entry alone is better, highest. That is the meaning.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Dhammapada 178, at [177] match). Read the Pali explanation of every verse in chapter XIII and Story XIII.11: the Pali on 178 glosses sole rule as a wheel-turning monarch’s rule and says the stream-fruit is best because a ruler of so much is still not freed from hell and the lower states, while the stream-enterer has the doors to the states of woe shut. The sentence carries exactly that; the story (Kala’s attainment surpassing a Universal Monarch and the worlds of gods and Brahma) agrees. Plain sense faithful (178 closes the chapter). entry-check ok.
